sentences.text:
Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 4 th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 4772 of 2024
 Smt. Bhagyashree And Others
 Versus
Sameer Khan And Others
Appearance:

Shri Shyamlal Patidar, learned counsel for the appell
 Shri Pankaj Kumar Jain, learned counsel for responden
 Insurance Company.

Order 
The appellants have filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 03.04.2024 passed by the learned Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dhar (M.P.) in MACC No.430/2022, whereby their claim filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act on account of the death of Deepak was rejected on the ground that the involvement of the insured vehicle was not proved.
2. The brief facts of the case are that on 24.04.2022, the deceased Deepak along with Anil Solanki and one Babulal had gone to village Lebad in connection with some electricity related work.
When they were returning to Ghata Billod near Lebad Square, Sameer Khan, a friend of Deepak met them.

Sameer took Deepak as a pillion rider on his motorcycle bearing registration number MP-13-DV-3437 and they proceeded towards Ghata NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35526 2 MA-4772-2024 Billod.
Sameer Khan was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, when they reached Mhow-Neemuch Road in front of the Moyra Factory, he rammed the motorcycle into a stationary barrow.
As a result, Deepak sustained grievous injuries on various parts of his body and died due to those injuries.
2.1 The claim petition was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Deepak.
Merg No.13/2020 was registered on 27.04.2022 under Section 174 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as Deepak had died during treatment on that date.

After about 40 days,
an FIR was lodged on 02.06.2022 stating that Deepak had died in the accident due to rash and negligent driving of Sameer Khan. The Claims Tribunal upon considering the evidence adduced in the appellants' petition filed under Section 166 of the Act, examined the matter in detail from paras 12 to 43 of the award and concluded that the vehicle in question i.e. the motorcycle bearing Smt. Bhagyashree vs Sameer Khan on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192144221/
1 registration number MP-13-DV-3437 was not proved to be involved in the accident.

Consequently,
the claim petition was rejected.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that in the discharge card of Deepak, it was mentioned that the injury was sustained due to a road traffic accident (RTA), which indicates that he died in a road accident.
He further submits that even in the criminal case, the involvement of the vehicle was found proved.
He also points out that there was an eyewitness to the accident, who deposed before the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the insured vehicle.

He thus submits that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35526 3 MA-4772-2024 Claims Tribunal erred in disbelieving the testimony of the eyewitness and the discharge card, both of which clearly indicated the involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident.
4. Opposing the submissions of the learned counsel for the appellants, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that it is a clear case of false implication of the insured vehicle.

He points out that the owner of the vehicle Sameer Khan has not suffered even a scratch in the accident in which Deepak has died and the story is that Sameer Khan was riding the motorcycle, Deepak was sitting as a pillion rider on the said motorcycle and Sameer rammed the bike into standing borrow.
He thus submits that it is impossible to have scenario where the rider has not sustained even the minor injury.

He then submits that this long delay of 40 days in lodging the FIR has to be seen in light of the fact that Sameer Khan is in the habit of providing his vehicle for claiming compensation against the Insurance Company in motor accident claim cases.

He points out that witness Neeraj Patela (NAW- 1) deposed before the Claims Tribunal that this same person i.e. Sameer Khan has offered his same vehicle for claiming compensation, the case number of the said matter was also provided in MACT Claim No.298/2022, thus, he pointed out that this vehicle has falsely been implanted after about 40 days of accident.
He thus supports the findings of the award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
6.

On perusal of the statement of Neeraj Patel (NAW-1), it becomes NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:35526 4 MA-4772-2024 clear that Sameer Khan, respondent No.1 has regularly been providing his vehicle as the offending vehicle in road traffic accident.
The witness pointed out that in MACT Claim No.298/2022 also, the very same vehicle was shown as the offending vehicle.

It is noteworthy that although Sameer Khan was alleged to be the rider of the motorcycle involved in the present accident, he did not suffer any injury, whereas Deepak, who was the pillion rider on the same motorcycle died.

It is also seen that the FIR was lodged after an unexplained delay of 40 days and during this entire period, there is complete absence of any material connecting the insured vehicle with the accident.
7.

The attempt made by the claimants to prove the incident by examining Anil Solanki (AW-2) as an eyewitness has lost significance in light of the answers given by him in cross-examination,
particularly in paras 11 and 12 of his deposition.

He clearly admitted that there is no mention in the Smt. Bhagyashree vs Sameer Khan on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192144221/
2 merg intimation about the road traffic accident or that Sameer Khan was riding the motorcycle.

He further stated that he was ahead by 100 meters from the motorcycle of Deepak, yet there is no mention of any fact suggesting that while he was trying to overtake the said motorcycle, the accident occurred.

8. Considering all these aspects, this Court is of the considered view that the Claims Tribunal has correctly assailed the evidence placed before it and has recorded impeccable findings in paras 12 to 43 of the award.
9. Accordingly, the present appeal being bereft of merit, is hereby dismissed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:35526 5 MA-4772-2024 Certified copy as per rules.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Anushree Smt. Bhagyashree vs Sameer Khan on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192144221/
